previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with metastatic cholangiocarcinoma on surveillance and a history of recurrent cholangitis due to multidrug-resistant E. coli, was admitted with fever and nausea. He had recently completed a four-week course of IV antibiotics for a hepatic abscess but had inadvertently stopped apixaban and ursodiol. On admission, he was restarted on ceftazidime-avibactam and metronidazole. MRI revealed new subcentimeter liver microabscesses. A multidisciplinary team decided to place a percutaneous transhepatic biliary drain to improve biliary drainage and prevent recurrence. A PICC line was placed for IV antibiotic administration. He was discharged home on a four-week course of IV and oral antibiotics, with plans for follow-up MRI and clinic visit. His portal vein thrombosis was managed with apixaban, and iron deficiency anemia was addressed with IV iron infusions.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ cholangioCA w/ h/o MDR E. Coli bacteremia ___ hepatic

malposition.// PTBD check/reposition/exchange

COMPARISON:  CT scan of the abdomen dated ___, PTB D placement
dated ___.

TECHNIQUE:  OPERATORS: Dr. ___ Interventional ___ and Dr.
___, Interventional Radiology fellow performed the procedure. Dr.
___ supervised the trainee during any key components of the
procedure where applicable and reviewed and agrees with the findings as
reported below.
ANESTHESIA: Moderate sedation was provided by administrating divided doses of
50mcg of fentanyl and 1 mg of midazolam throughout the total intra-service
time of 5 minutes during which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were
continuously monitored by an independent trained radiology nurse. 1% lidocaine
was injected in the skin and subcutaneous tissues overlying the access site.
MEDICATIONS: 1 g ceftriaxone
CONTRAST: 10 ml of Optiray contrast
FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE: 2.3 minutes, 17 mGy

PROCEDURE:
1. Cholangiogram through existing right percutaneous transhepatic biliary
drainage access.
2. Exchange of the existing right percutaneous transhepatic biliary drainage
catheter with a new 12 ___ PTBD catheter.
PROCEDURE DETAILS:
Following the discussion of the risks, benefits and alternatives to the
procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the patient. The patient
was then brought to the angiography suite and placed prone on the exam table.
A pre-procedure time-out was performed per ___ protocol.

The site was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.  Maximal barrier
technique including hand hygiene, eye wear protection, gloves, sterile gown,
blue drape, face mask and head cap were utilized.  Contrast was injected
through the indwelling tube.  The tube was cut, stay sutures were released and
___ wire was advanced into the small bowel through the tube.  A new 12
___ biliary drain was destrung, flushed and advanced over the wire.  The
wire and inner dilator were removed, the pigtail was partially formed in the
duodenum.  Contrast was injected confirming appropriate positioning.  The
catheter was sutured to the skin and secured with a StatLock.  Sterile
dressing was applied.  The drain was connected to a bag.  The patient
tolerated the procedure without any complications.

FINDINGS:


1. Cholangiogram through the indwelling drain demonstrates opacification of
some of the right and left intrahepatic biliary ducts with spillage of
contrast from the drain in the hilum into the metallic stents of the common
bile duct to flow into the small bowel.  The does not appear to be direct
passage of contrast through the indwelling drain from the hilum to the
small-bowel.
2. Cholangiogram through the new tube demonstrates passage of contrast through
the drain into the small bowel without opacification of intrahepatic biliary
ducts or spillage into the metallic stents.

IMPRESSION:


1. Successful exchange and upsize of right percutaneous transhepatic biliary
drain from a 10 ___ to a 12 ___ drain.
